title: Latent Decision Flow Rewards for Clinical Guideline Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.38709v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Clinical practice guidelines encode evidence-based recommendations as conditional decision flows, which makes them a natural source of process supervision for training reasoning models. Two properties of clinical reasoning make this supervision difficult to use. A decision flow consistent with a guideline does not by itself determine the correct answer for a given patient, which we call the path--answer gap, and several valid decision flows can support the same clinical decision, which we call path multiplicity. Current training approaches address parts of this problem. Answer rewards supervise the final decision, and process rewards computed against a reference flow supervise one valid decision flow per case. Supervised fine-tuning on annotated flows teaches guideline-consistent reasoning but constrains the model to one trajectory per case and can reduce answer accuracy. We introduce GUIDER, a method that jointly optimizes a decision

translated_title: 用于临床指南推理的潜在决策流奖励
translated_abstract: 临床实践指南将基于证据的推荐编码为条件决策流，这使其成为训练推理模型的过程监督的天然来源。然而，临床推理的两个特性使得这种监督难以利用：其一，与指南一致的决策流本身并不能确定针对特定患者的正确答案，我们将其称为“路径—答案鸿沟”；其二，多个有效的决策流可以支持同一个临床决策，我们将其称为“路径多样性”。当前的训练方法仅部分解决了这一问题：答案奖励只监督最终决策，而基于参考流计算的过程奖励只能监督每个病例中单一的有效决策流；在标注流上进行监督微调能够教会模型遵循指南的推理，但会将模型限制为每个病例仅一条轨迹，并可能降低答案准确率。我们提出了GUIDER，这是一种联合优化决策……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了GUIDER方法，通过潜在决策流奖励联合优化推理过程与最终答案，以解决临床指南推理中“路径—答案鸿沟”和“路径多样性”两大难题。
en_tdlr: GUIDER introduces latent decision flow rewards to jointly optimize reasoning processes and final answers, tackling the path–answer gap and path multiplicity challenges in clinical guideline reasoning.
